name: Ohio
overview: Ohio mostly sells tax-delinquent real estate outright after a tax foreclosure. A court orders the parcel sold, and the county sheriff sells it, usually online through the state's sheriff sale auction site run by RealAuction under a state contract. In a tax foreclosure the minimum bid can be the taxes, assessments, penalties, interest and costs owed rather than the usual two-thirds of appraised value. Parcels left unsold after two sales are forfeited to the state, and the county auditor can later offer them at a forfeited land sale. Some county treasurers also sell tax certificates (liens): at a public auction, bidding starts at 18% simple interest per year and goes down. Some counties, such as Franklin, instead sell their certificates in bulk as a portfolio.

counties.office: Cuyahoga County Sheriff's Department, Civil Division
counties.next_sale_note: No specific sale dates or recurring sale day are posted on the official pages read. The Sheriff assigns each sale date roughly six weeks after an order of sale. An older county 'topics' page (https://cuyahogacounty.gov/topics/foreclosure-sales) says 'Foreclosure sales are conducted every Monday at 9:00 a.m.' at the Justice Center, but it conflicts with the current online-only pages and is treated as outdated.
counties.how_to_bid: All sheriff foreclosure sales, tax-delinquent ones included, are held online only through the county's RealAuction site, where bidders register and must meet RealAuction's terms. Buyers of tax-delinquent properties must file an Affidavit of Non-delinquency for each property. Payment goes to the Sheriff's Civil Division by certified or cashier's check, money order or law firm check.

counties.how_to_bid: Since March 12, 2026 all sheriff's sales, tax foreclosures included, are online only through the RealAuction site, where bidders register and pay deposits electronically. The starting bid is the delinquent taxes and costs, and the deposit is 10% of the starting bid (minimum $1,000, maximum $5,000) under Local Rule 5.02(D)(1). Tax foreclosure bidders must submit a notarized delinquent tax affidavit (R.C. 5721.19(J)) by 10:00 AM on the Wednesday before the Thursday auction. Properties are sold as is with no title guarantee.

The page gives two times and places: the upcoming-sales notice says 10:00 A.M. at the Arts Hall Building, Stark County Fair Grounds, while the Tax Foreclosure Sales section says 9:00 A.M. in the Event Hall of the Stark County Office Building; confirm with the Sheriff before attending. counties.how_to_bid: Monthly delinquent tax sales are in person. The minimum bid covers the taxes owed through the sale date plus case costs, not other lien holders' amounts. The winning bidder pays a 10% deposit to the Treasurer's Office by 4:30 P.M. on sale day (cashier's or certified check) and the balance within 30 days of the filing of the confirmation of sale; bring the name for the deed, a tax mailing address, a phone number and ID. A sale with no bids is rescheduled to the first Tuesday of the following month. Tax certificate foreclosures (private attorney) are sold online through RealAuction: register there and post a $1,000, $5,000 or $10,000 deposit per property by wire or ACH before the Monday auction. Sales are as is, and properties are not open for inspection.

The balance is due by certified or cashier's check within 30 days of the Sheriff's notice after the confirmation of sale, plus recording and conveyance fees. Sales are as is, and the Sheriff does not show properties.
